Replies.Text:
**Build log, Step 6: Licensing** (built by Claude Fable 5.1 as Claude-CLI, 2026-10-25; nothing committed).

**What was built**

- **The tiers in Clerk** (`src/Roles.js`, `src/Clerk.js`, `src/Operations.js`, `src/Api.js`): the plans are `personal` and `professional`, lower case as the metadata holds them, `PLANS` ranking professional above personal; Owners and Members need personal, the Administrator professional; the old names Host and User are not read (a claim carrying one is no license), the readme and the Clerk subplan (revision 10, its license section) say so. The three sign-in checks keep their places and read the new names; the Scope Public refusal says "a Professional license is required"; the drag refusal names the tier with a capital.
- **What each tier enforces.** Free: the Desktop on local folders and the sidecar, the task buttons disabled with "a Personal license" (Step 4's rule, on the new names), Add host and Open host on the chooser disabled with the reason, Start the Server Host disabled. Personal: the task buttons, Connect to Host (`connect_host_here` refuses below it), Start the Server Host with Scope Local, the Host's pages. Professional: the Host keeps its file's Scope (Public allowed) when the Desktop starts it, and is the Administrator of a Public server. The Host refuses Public at bind time below professional when a tier is given (`Server.Start( { Tier } )`, one line naming the tier): the Desktop passes its cached tier to its headless form; the headless `consensus serve` and the image pass none and listen as their file says, admitting licensed sign-ins alone, as the Clerk subplan has it.
- **The Desktop signs in** (`desktop/License.js` new, `desktop/Settings.js`, `desktop/main.js`, `preload.js`, `public/js/session.js`, `title-bar.js`, `help.js`, `index.html`): Sign in… in the page's menu loads ClerkJS and shows the box as the Settings popup's button does; a signed-in session's token goes to the desktop (`ConsensusDesktop.SetLicense`, on every load of the page signed in), which verifies it against the instance's keys as a server does (`License.Verify` over `src/Clerk.js`) and writes desktop.json's `License: { Plan, Until, Checked }`; `License.Tier` says the tier the Desktop is at: the plan while Checked is within 14 days and Until has not passed, Free otherwise, with `Lapsed` saying why; the page reads it through `Session.Tier()` and `Licensed()` (the boot info carries it, so it holds offline), About shows `License.Line` ("Personal, checked 3 days ago: 11 days left offline"; "Free: the Personal license last checked on … is more than 14 days old; sign in again to renew it"; "Free: the … license ran out on …"; "Free: no license"), and Sign out clears the cache before the reload. A verified sign-in with no license clears it too. Free needs no account.
- **Connecting to a Host** is unchanged: the page sends the session token to its own server as a browser does, and a Host's own checks apply.
- **The pricing page** `docs/pricing.html` names Free, Personal and Professional with what each grants, from the plan's Licensing section, and says prices are not set yet; `features.md` links it.

**Decided during the build**

- The bind-time check runs on a tier the Desktop gives; a Host started headless or in the image has no tier and starts as before. Checking at bind is the one place for the Desktop, the sign-in checks staying for the servers, as the plan says the API keeps them.
- The Desktop verifies the token itself (signature, exp, nbf, issuer; no azp, the page having no host) rather than trusting the page's reading of the claims.
- A sign-in is reported to the desktop on every signed-in load of the page, which is "asks Clerk again when the window opens online"; offline, the cache stands.
- The chooser's Hosts are disabled on Free with the reason in the button's title, and Start the Server Host is disabled in both menus; the readme and the pricing page say what each tier grants.
- The Desktop's own menu holds Sign in… and Sign out beside Reload; the account menu the plan names is Clerk's user button, which already offers sign-out.
- `bin/docs.js` writes a Personal license into the pictures' desktop.json, so the chooser's Open host is enabled there.

**Tests**

- `test/Clerk.test.js`: the license tests on the new names; the old names, and a capitalised one, refused.
- `test/Api.test.js`: the Clerk test on the new names (the sign-in checks with each tier); a new test: Public refused at bind with a personal or free tier, the line naming the tier, started with professional and with no tier, Local needing none; `ROLES.PLANS` and the ranks.
- `test/Desktop.test.js`: the license with a generated key pair as the Clerk tests do: a token verified into the record, the organization's higher plan, an old name, no license, another key and a bad token refused; the tier within 14 days, at the edge and past it, Until passed, nothing cached, an old name cached; `AtLeast`; the About lines; desktop.json keeping, dropping and clearing the field.
- `test/ClerkSmoke.test.js`: the desktop case waits for the cached tier and reads desktop.json's License after the sign-in (with the keys set; skipped here).
- `test/Ui.test.js` and `bin/smoke.js` read the new names.
- Results: the non-browser suite 190 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped (the Clerk smokes without keys); the browser UI test 45 pass (on a second run alone: the first run beside the suite lost the two known load-sensitive tests and my new collapsible check, which now reads the project's open state first); the Docs test 2 pass; npm run smoke SMOKE OK with 64 checks (its menu check now takes the Sign in… item).

**Docs**: the readme's license paragraph rewritten for the tiers and the Desktop's sign-in; `docs/guide/features.md`, `settings.md` and `sharing.md` name the Professional license; the sign-in box's text; `docs/pricing.html` new; the Clerk subplan's license section brought in line (revision 10); the guide rebuilt.

Resolve to accept; I then apply this thread, commit as "Rearchitecturation Step 6: Licensing" and set the Subplan to Plan. A reply means fix and report again.
